```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6)
has <- function(...) all(vapply(c(...), requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE))
```

With single-cell data, every step of the LocusPick workflow gains a
**cell-type** dimension:

| Step | Bulk | Single cell |
|---|---|---|
| Differential expression | DESeq2/edgeR results | **pseudobulk** DE per cell type (`pseudobulkDE()`) |
| Signal tracks | bigWigs per condition | accessibility per cell type × condition, from the fragments file (`scSignal()`) |
| Peak → gene | nearest gene | **peak-gene links** from multiome data when available, else nearest gene |
| Groups and ranking | per group | per cell type × group |
| Plots | tracks + expression | all cell types' tracks (shared y-axis) + pseudobulk expression of the locus's cell type |

`scLocusPick()` runs all of it. It accepts:

* **multiome** data (RNA and ATAC from the same cells): one Seurat object
  with an RNA assay and a Signac `ChromatinAssay`, a Cell Ranger ARC output
  folder, or matrices;
* **unpaired** scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq of the same samples: two objects (or
  folders) whose metadata share cell-type, sample and condition columns.

Supported inputs: Seurat (with Signac), Bioconductor `SingleCellExperiment`,
Cell Ranger / Cell Ranger ATAC / Cell Ranger ARC folders (`read10x()`), and
plain count matrices with a metadata table.

## Example data

```{r}
library(LocusPick)
sc <- locusPickSingleCellExample()
table(sc$meta$cell_type, paste(sc$meta$genotype, sc$meta$age))
```

The synthetic data have 8 samples (WT/KO × young/old, 2 replicates each) and
two cell types. In hepatocytes, *geneA* is activated by the factor (lower in
KO) and falls with age, and accessibility at its promoter drops with age.
Kupffer cells show no changes but have their own open site near *geneF*.

## One call

```{r, eval = has("DESeq2", "Rsamtools")}
res <- scLocusPick(
    sc$rna, atac = NULL,                      # matrices here; see below for objects
    cellType = "cell_type", sample = "sample",
    perturbation = c("genotype", "KO", "WT"), # test / reference
    condition    = c("age", "old", "young"),
    genes = sc$genes, peaks = sc$peaks, links = sc$links,
    fragments = sc$fragments, meta = sc$meta, atacMeta = sc$meta)
res
```

```{r singlecell-plot, eval = has("DESeq2", "Rsamtools")}
plot(res, "geneA")
```

The tracks show every cell type and condition on one shared y-axis, so the
cell-type specificity of a site is visible. The inset shows pseudobulk
expression (CPM) in the locus's cell type for every genotype × age group.
`reportLoci(res, "review.pdf")` writes all top loci and the candidate table.

Kupffer cells have no candidates here because no gene is differentially
expressed in them. That is reported, not hidden.

## With Seurat + Signac objects

For a multiome object, everything is taken from the object: RNA counts from
the default assay (or `RNA` if the default holds peaks), peaks, fragment files
and the barcode mapping from the chromatin assay, and peak-gene links from
`Links()` if you ran `Signac::LinkPeaks()`.

```{r, eval = has("Signac", "SeuratObject", "DESeq2", "Rsamtools"), message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
so <- locusPickSingleCellExample(seurat = TRUE)$object
so
```

```{r, eval = has("Signac", "SeuratObject", "DESeq2", "Rsamtools")}
res2 <- scLocusPick(so, cellType = "cell_type", sample = "sample",
                    perturbation = c("genotype", "KO", "WT"),
                    condition = c("age", "old", "young"),
                    genes = sc$genes)
res2$top[, c("group", "gene", "peak_id", "link_score", "score")]
```

For **unpaired** data, pass the two objects:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
res <- scLocusPick(rna_obj, atac = atac_obj,
                   cellType = "cell_type", sample = "sample",
                   perturbation = c("genotype", "KO", "WT"),
                   condition = c("age", "old", "young"),
                   genes = "gencode.vM25.annotation.gtf",
                   orgDb = org.Mm.eg.db::org.Mm.eg.db)
```

Without peak-gene links (they need RNA and ATAC from the same cells), peaks are
assigned to the nearest gene. Cell-type labels must use the same names in both
objects; label transfer between modalities (e.g. Seurat's
`TransferData()`) is the usual way to get there.

## Other inputs

`SingleCellExperiment` objects work like Seurat objects, using the `counts`
assay by default; give the fragments file and, if the ATAC data are a separate
object, its metadata:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
res <- scLocusPick(sce_rna, atac = NULL, cellType = "celltype", sample = "donor",
                   condition = c("treatment", "drug", "vehicle"),
                   genes = "genes.gtf", peaks = "peaks.bed",
                   fragments = "fragments.tsv.gz", atacMeta = colData(sce_atac))
```

Cell Ranger output folders are read with `read10x()`. Cell Ranger does not
know your cell types or samples, so add a metadata table with one row per
barcode (from your clustering):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
arc <- read10x("sample1/outs")                  # Cell Ranger ARC (multiome)
arc
res <- scLocusPick(arc, cellType = "cell_type", sample = "sample",
                   condition = c("age", "old", "young"),
                   genes = "genes.gtf", meta = my_annotations)
```

For several samples, aggregate them first (`cellranger-arc aggr`) or merge them
into one object; `fragmentSource()` also accepts several fragment files with
one barcode list per file.

## Step by step

### Pseudobulk differential expression

```{r, eval = has("DESeq2")}
pb <- pseudobulk(sc$rna, sample = "sample", cellType = "cell_type", meta = sc$meta)
pb
de <- pseudobulkDE(pb, contrast = c("genotype", "KO", "WT"), covariates = "age")
de
head(de$Hepatocyte, 4)
```

`pseudobulkDE()` uses the object's default assay unless `assay` is given, and
can also take the object directly. Each result is a normal LocusPick DE table,
so it plugs into `defineGroups()`. Your own DE results can be used instead:
pass a table (used for every cell type) or a named list of tables per cell
type as `perturbation` or `condition`.

### Accessibility tracks

```{r, eval = has("Rsamtools")}
tracks <- scSignal(NULL, groupBy = c("cell_type", "age"),
                   fragments = sc$fragments, meta = sc$meta)
signalAtPeaks(sc$peaks[c(1, 7)], tracks)[, c("peak_id", "Hepatocyte_young_mean",
                                             "Hepatocyte_old_mean", "Kupffer_young_mean")]
```

Coverage is counted from the fragments of each group's cells and scaled per
million fragments. When the metadata hold a per-cell fragment count
(`atac_fragments`, `passed_filters`) or in-peak count (`nCount_ATAC`), it is
used as the total; otherwise the fragments file is read once to count it.

### Peak-gene links

Links are used as the peak-gene assignment when available. They can come from
`Signac::Links()` or any table with a `peak` (`"chr-start-end"`) and `gene`
column:

```{r}
cand <- buildCandidates(sc$peaks, sc$genes, groups = NULL, links = sc$links)
cand[, c("gene", "peak_id", "link_score", "distance", "near_gene")]
```

Links longer than `maxLinkDist` (default 500 kb) are flagged.

## Things to watch

* **Use pseudobulk DE.** Cell-level tests (e.g. Seurat `FindMarkers()`) treat
  every cell as a replicate and give inflated p-values. `readDE()` reads their
  output but warns. Pseudobulk DE needs at least two biological samples per
  condition (`minSamples`); cell types without them are skipped with a message.
* **Adjust for other factors.** In a two-factor design, each contrast is
  adjusted for the other automatically. When testing only one, list the other
  sample-level factors in `covariates`. In the example, testing age alone
  without adjusting for genotype finds no significant genes.
* **Use raw counts.** Pseudobulk sums raw counts. The `SCT` assay holds
  corrected counts; prefer the `RNA` assay (LocusPick reports which one it uses).
* **Cell numbers.** Pseudobulks and tracks from fewer than `minCells` cells
  are dropped. Rare cell types give noisy tracks.
* **Global shifts.** As in bulk data, check `res$shift`: if accessibility
  falls with age at most peaks in a cell type, a track showing the same fall at
  an example is not specific to it.
